q: How does urea from coal gasification at Talcher compare on CO2 with gas based urea?
title: Talcher coal gasification urea: CO2
short: Coal gasification makes ammonia from coal instead of natural gas, and coal carries far more carbon per unit of hydrogen. Expect a much higher figure per tonne of urea than gas based plants unless CO2 is captured and stored. Count it from coal invoices and carbon content, not a flat factor.
audience: Fertiliser makers, policy teams and buyers following the Talcher coal gasification urea project

ol: Coal fed to gasifiers and boilers, in tonnes, with carbon content.
Subtract carbon leaving in ash or slag.
CO2 used to make urea is still counted as emitted under CBAM.

p: CO2 captured and permanently stored lowers the figure. CO2 sold for another use generally does not.
Urea is a CBAM good, so any EU export would carry this figure. Most Indian urea serves the home market.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel, electricity and freight invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record per site, so each figure you send a buyer traces back to the documents behind it.

sources.label: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories
